problem: Semantic-map-based ObjectNav predictors are trained on only hundreds of scanned scene-level semantic maps (MP3D, HM3DSem), because 3D scanning and annotation are costly. Procedural datasets like ProcTHOR rely on hand-designed rules and show a domain gap, and trajectory-only augmentation adds no new floorplan structures.
motivation: The map predictor only needs pairs of partial and full semantic maps, not photorealistic 3D reconstructions, so map pairs can be generated directly at scale. Composing real-home floorplans with room-level maps from real scans should keep real structural and semantic regularities while scaling data.
key_idea: Generate large-scale (partial, full) semantic map training pairs by filling real-home floorplan rooms with category-matched room semantic/obstacle maps from MP3D/HM3DSem, then deriving partial maps via visibility-aware ray casting (VisRC).
insight: With a fixed map budget, more distinct floorplans beat more room recompositions (K saturates at 8 to 16, both 64.3 SR at 24k floorplans) and beat more trajectories per scene (flat curve), which suggests inter-room structure matters because other rooms cannot be inspected cheaply. Room-category correctness matters a lot (manual 64.3 vs LLM 59.4 vs random 44.2 SR). VisRC beats area-matched crops (64.3 vs 60.8 SR), and swapping segmented for GT training labels changes results little while segmented test labels cost about 6 SR.
method: Inter-room scaling: collect 12,794 real-estate properties, giving 24,000 floorplans; extract room masks from SVG and manually label them into 12 categories (~1,300 human-hours); 301,663 base room masks.

Intra-room scaling: build a library of 1,364 MP3D rooms and 1,186 HM3DSem v0.1 rooms (semantic + 2.5D obstacle heightmaps at 5 cm), and for each floorplan sample K=8 category-matched room-map combinations.
Fit and validate: align and scale-to-fit room maps into masks (reject scale ratio >1.5) and check navigable connectivity, resampling invalid compositions; this yields 192,000 full maps.
Trajectory sampling: follow PONI, using shortest paths between random start and end points in each composed map.

VisRC: ray casting with FOV 79°, range 5 m, and eye height 0.88 m against the obstacle heightmap gives the visible region; the union along the path gives the explored map, which masks the full semantic and obstacle maps into partial maps M_t (4+N channels). Explored-region IoU with RGB-D accumulation is 0.89.

Predictor training: unchanged PEANUT PSPNet, with 300k iterations, batch size 64, warmup and cosine LR schedule; for MP3D adds Stubborn mapping, RFS + Seesaw loss for the segmenter, and multi-frame target confirmation.

setting.backbone: PEANUT PSPNet map predictor (trained from scratch on NaviScale maps) + Mask R-CNN (HM3D) / RedNet (MP3D) segmentation + FMM planning
setting.training_data: NaviScale: 192,000 composed semantic maps from 24,000 real-home floorplans with room maps from MP3D and HM3DSem v0.1 training splits, one sampled trajectory per map
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D with semantic segmentation projected into a top-down semantic map (5 cm cells)
setting.action_space: discrete low-level actions (stop, forward, turn left/right, look up/down); long-term goal predicted on the map, FMM planning
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D and MP3D ObjectNav) plus a real robot
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT semantic labels only in a supplementary analysis)

numbers.extra: 300k updated schedule; five-run mean; 20 val scenes, 2000 episodes

results: On HM3D, NaviScale reaches 64.3 SR / 34.8 SPL, above GLMap (62.7 SR) and TrajRAG. On MP3D it reaches 43.1 SR, the highest listed, though G3D-LF has higher SPL (18.8). Holding architecture and protocol fixed, swapping the original training data for NaviScale gives +4.7 SR on HM3D and +2.8 SR on MP3D. It also beats ProcTHOR (55.2 SR) and MP3D+HM3D (61.9 SR), and real-robot success improves from 58.3 to 75.0 (S1) and from 40.0 to 60.0 (S2).
limitations: Increasing K only recombines existing MP3D/HM3D source rooms, so rare arrangements stay underrepresented; the dataset is residential (mostly North American) and static.
Part of the gain comes from the longer training and inference protocol changes, and the partial-map ablation is confounded by the larger observed area of the room-visible condition.
Real-robot evaluation is small (32 episodes, 2 sites); the floorplan labeling needs ~1,300 human-hours; MP3D SPL is below G3D-LF.
